the model says the meaning changed: Regressions are now skipped when the failing run's closure hash differs from the current one, so an edited test (EX-4) or a failure made stale by a later source change (EX-7, EX-10) no longer counts as a regression, which the requirement says it still is.; brought to the owner as a card: You want a regression to hold the merge until it is fixed, and the requirement agrees: a failure stays until a run passes it, even if the code changes again and nothing is rerun.

The change makes the regression list skip any failure recorded on code that differs from what this checkout has now. Its stated aim is reasonable: a failure from another worktree, read through the shared test history, should not count as a regression here. But the check can't tell that case apart from a failure in this same checkout followed by another edit. That failure would also drop off the list, which conflicts with the rule that a failure stays until a run passes it. A failing test could then stop counting as a regression just because the code was edited again.

What is unclear is whether this was wanted. No request from you is on record for this change, and the requirement doesn't say how failures from another worktree should be treated. The diff also doesn't show whether another part of the merge check would still hold that edited-after-failure case, for example as a stale failure or an unverified test. So I can't tell whether this is a real break or an acceptable narrowing, and I'm not sending it back as a plain mistake.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the aim, narrow the change: ignore only failures from another worktree, so a failure here stays until a run passes it") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the change as it is and reword the requirement: a failure on code that has since changed is no longer a regression, as long as the merge still holds until a rerun") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change: every recorded failure counts as a regression wherever it came from, until a run passes it") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-254#7 --consequences "..." --why "...")
